description:
## Why this issue exists

Two nearly-identical SSRF guard functions exist in different modules:
- `is_valid_tailscale_host()` in kithd/src/transport.rs
- `is_valid_fetch_host()` in kithd/src/peer_fetch.rs

Both reject private RFC-1918 ranges, loopback, metadata IPs (169.254.x), and require the host to look like a valid Tailscale node name or IP. The implementations are similar but not identical — they can diverge independently, meaning a security fix applied to one may not be applied to the other.

This is especially risky because SSRF guards are security-critical: a missed case in either copy can be exploited to reach internal services.

## What needs to be done

Consolidate into a single `is_valid_tailscale_host()` function in `kith-core` or a shared internal module. Both `transport.rs` and `peer_fetch.rs` should call the same function. Add a unit test suite for the consolidated function that covers: loopback, RFC-1918, 169.254/16, 100.64/10 (CGNAT), valid Tailscale IP, valid node name.

## Acceptance criteria

- One canonical SSRF host-validation function used by both outbound HTTP paths
- Removing the duplicate eliminates divergence risk
- The shared function has tests covering all rejected and accepted address classes
title: SSRF host-validation logic duplicated in peer_fetch and transport
